title: Merge k Sorted Lists
statement: Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list and return its head.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(53)
    return [[sorted(r.randint(0, 10**6) for _ in range(50)) for _ in range(2000)]]

hints.1_question: At any moment the next output node is the smallest among the heads of all lists. Which structure finds a minimum quickly?
hints.2_nudge: Put each list's head in a min-heap; pop the smallest, append it, and push its successor.
hints.3_big_hint: heap items (val, list_index, node) so ties never compare nodes. Pop, attach, push node.next if it exists.

known_bugs.name: heap compares nodes on equal values (TypeError)
known_bugs.followup: When two heap entries have equal values, what does Python try to compare next, and can it compare ListNodes?

known_bugs.name: merges lists one after another (O(k * N))
known_bugs.followup: How long is the accumulated result when you merge the 2000th list into it? How many times do you re-walk early nodes?

known_bugs.name: assumes at least one list is given
known_bugs.followup: What should you return when the input list of lists is empty?

followups: How does divide-and-conquer pairwise merging compare?
Why is the index needed in the heap tuple?
